- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, it often overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1.2x the prior 7-day average.
- In low-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment < -0.30), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model consistently underestimates 30-day horizon in high volatility periods; apply 1.1–1.2x multiplier to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.50 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.5 to -0.5 in 3–5 days), model often lags; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >1.5σ above recent 14-day mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment remains positive for 3+ consecutive days.
